/usr/local/google/home/warrenzhu/github/rudis/src/conn_balance.rs:
    1|       |//! Connection load balancing across shards.
    2|       |//!
    3|       |//! Each shard binds its own listener with `SO_REUSEPORT`, which means the
    4|       |//! *kernel* chooses the owning shard by hashing the connection 4-tuple. For a
    5|       |//! loopback client the source IP, destination IP and destination port are all
    6|       |//! constant, so the only varying input is the client's ephemeral source port.
    7|       |//! Shard assignment is therefore a random ball-into-bins draw, re-rolled on
    8|       |//! every reconnect.
    9|       |//!
   10|       |//! With 64 connections over 16 shards the busiest shard receives ~8 while
   11|       |//! others receive 1-2, and since throughput is gated by the most loaded shard
   12|       |//! the server runs at roughly half its ideal capacity. Measured: 2.74M ops/s at
   13|       |//! 64 connections versus 5.44M at 256 connections on an otherwise identical
   14|       |//! configuration, matching a Monte-Carlo prediction of 51.9% of ideal.
   15|       |//!
   16|       |//! Deferring `accept()` on an overloaded shard does **not** help: `SO_REUSEPORT`
   17|       |//! commits the connection to a specific listener's accept queue at SYN time, so
   18|       |//! an unaccepted connection simply waits there rather than being redistributed.
   19|       |//!
   20|       |//! This module instead balances explicitly. After accepting, a shard consults
   21|       |//! the global per-shard connection census and, if it is carrying more than the
   22|       |//! least loaded shard, hands the raw fd over to that shard. All shards are
   23|       |//! threads in a single process and share one fd table, so the transfer is just
   24|       |//! an integer -- no `SCM_RIGHTS` required.
   25|       |//!
   26|       |//! # Thread-per-core compliance
   27|       |//!
   28|       |//! The atomics here are touched exactly twice per connection: once on accept
   29|       |//! and once on close. They are **not** on the per-command hot data path, which
   30|       |//! remains free of shared state.
   31|       |

  119|       |/// Number of times [`claim_owner`] re-scans before giving up and keeping the
  120|       |/// connection locally. Bounds the retry loop so a hot census cannot livelock
  121|       |/// the accept path; keeping one connection on a slightly busier shard is a far
  122|       |/// cheaper outcome than stalling accepts.
  123|       |const MAX_CLAIM_RETRIES: usize = 4;
  124|       |
  125|       |/// Choose the shard that will own a freshly accepted connection **and reserve
  126|       |/// its census slot**, returning that shard.
  127|       |///
  128|       |/// The reservation is the whole point. During a client's connection burst every
  129|       |/// shard is accepting in parallel, so if the count only rose once the target
  130|       |/// adopted the connection, the target would appear idle for the entire in-flight
  131|       |/// window and every other shard would independently choose it, reproducing the
  132|       |/// imbalance this module exists to remove.
  133|       |///
  134|       |/// The claim is a single `compare_exchange` against the count that was observed
  135|       |/// during the scan, so two shards racing for the same target cannot both win:
  136|       |/// the loser sees a stale value, re-scans, and picks the next least loaded
  137|       |/// shard.
  138|       |///
  139|       |/// The caller owns the returned reservation and must eventually call
  140|       |/// [`unregister_conn`] for that shard, whether the connection runs to completion
  141|       |/// or is abandoned.
  142|    792|pub fn claim_owner(accepting_shard: usize, num_shards: usize) -> usize {

  300|       |        // this module. There, the accept loop only decided on a target and the

  345|      1|    fn test_claim_owner_is_race_free_under_concurrent_accepts() {
  346|       |        // Concurrency stress: all shards accept in parallel during a client's
  347|       |        // connection burst, so claims race. This checks that the
  348|       |        // compare_exchange placement never loses or double counts a claim and

  354|       |        // actually mattered in production was cross-thread and far wider. The
  355|       |        // guard against that is

 1951|    493|fn recycle_conn_scratch(mut s: ConnScratch) {
 1952|       |    // A remote shard holds an Arc clone of a BatchResponder for as long as its batch
 1953|       |    // is in flight, and writes the payload cross-thread through an UnsafeCell in
 1954|       |    // BatchResponder::finish(). If this connection tore down (client hang-up, write
 1955|       |    // error) while a batch was still outstanding, handing that responder to the next
 1956|       |    // connection would let the late finish() deliver another client's results, or
 1957|       |    // leave a stale ready=true that desyncs the new harvest loop. Only pool scratch
 1958|       |    // whose responders are provably unreferenced and idle; otherwise drop it and let
 1959|       |    // the straggling shard release the Arc normally.
 1960|    493|    let reusable = s
 1961|    493|        .responders

17903|      1|        assert!(recovered.is_empty());
17904|      1|        assert!(!recovered.try_reclaim(64));
17905|      1|        drop(cmd);

17907|      1|        assert_eq!(recovered.capacity(), 64);

17910|       |    #[test]
17911|      1|    fn test_conn_scratch_pool_reuse_and_inflight_responder_guard() {
17912|       |        // Drain anything a previous test on this thread may have pooled.
17913|      1|        CONN_SCRATCH_POOL.with(|p| p.borrow_mut().clear());
17914|       |
17915|       |        // 1. An idle scratch round-trips through the pool and reuses its allocations.
17916|      1|        let mut scratch = take_conn_scratch(4);
17917|      1|        assert_eq!(scratch.responders.len(), 4);
17918|      1|        let out_ptr = scratch.out_buf.as_ptr();
17919|      1|        scratch.out_buf.extend_from_slice(b"+OK\r\n");
17920|      1|        scratch
17921|      1|            .commands
17922|      1|            .push(Command::Get(Bytes::from_static(b"k")));
17923|      1|        recycle_conn_scratch(scratch);
17924|       |
17925|      1|        let reused = take_conn_scratch(4);
17926|      1|        assert!(reused.out_buf.is_empty(), "pooled out_buf must be cleared");
17927|      1|        assert!(
17928|      1|            reused.commands.is_empty(),
17929|       |            "pooled commands must be cleared"
17930|       |        );
17931|      1|        assert_eq!(
17932|      1|            reused.out_buf.as_ptr(),
17933|       |            out_ptr,
17934|       |            "pooled scratch must reuse the same heap allocation"
17935|       |        );
17936|       |
17937|       |        // 2. Scratch whose responder is still referenced by an in-flight remote shard
17938|       |        //    batch must NOT be pooled, or a late finish() would write another client's
17939|       |        //    results into the next connection's responder.
17940|      1|        let inflight = std::sync::Arc::clone(&reused.responders[2]);
17941|      1|        recycle_conn_scratch(reused);
17942|      1|        CONN_SCRATCH_POOL.with(|p| {
17943|      1|            assert!(
17944|      1|                p.borrow().is_empty(),
17945|       |                "scratch with an outstanding responder Arc must not be pooled"
17946|       |            );
17947|      1|        });
17948|      1|        drop(inflight);
17949|       |
17950|       |        // 3. Scratch carrying an unharvested ready=true payload must also be rejected.
17951|      1|        let stale = take_conn_scratch(4);
17952|      1|        stale.responders[1].state.0.store(
17953|       |            crate::mailbox::BATCH_COMPLETED,
17954|      1|            std::sync::atomic::Ordering::Release,
17955|       |        );
17956|      1|        recycle_conn_scratch(stale);
17957|      1|        CONN_SCRATCH_POOL.with(|p| {
17958|      1|            assert!(
17959|      1|                p.borrow().is_empty(),
17960|       |                "scratch with a stale ready responder must not be pooled"
17961|       |            );
17962|      1|        });
17963|       |
17964|       |        // 4. A different shard count never aliases a pooled entry.
17965|      1|        let clean = take_conn_scratch(4);
17966|      1|        recycle_conn_scratch(clean);
17967|      1|        let other = take_conn_scratch(8);
17968|      1|        assert_eq!(other.responders.len(), 8);
17969|      1|        assert_eq!(other.remote_batches.len(), 8);
17970|      1|        recycle_conn_scratch(other);
17971|      1|    }

18080|       |    #[test]
18081|      1|    fn test_squashed_pending_bitmask_polling() {
18082|      1|        let responder = std::sync::Arc::new(crate::mailbox::BatchResponder::new());
18083|      1|        let mut resp_slot = [crate::shard::CompactResp::NULL; 4];
18084|      1|        responder.prepare(resp_slot.as_mut_ptr());
18085|       |
18086|      1|        let mut pending_mask: u64 = 0b101; // shards 0 and 2
18087|      1|        let responders = [responder.clone(), responder.clone(), responder.clone()];
18088|       |
18089|       |        // Finish shard 0
18090|      1|        responder.finish(vec![]);
18091|      1|        let mut check_mask = pending_mask;
18092|      3|        while check_mask != 0 {
18093|      2|            let target_shard = check_mask.trailing_zeros() as usize;
18094|      2|            if target_shard == 0 {
18095|      1|                let r = &responders[target_shard];
18096|      1|                if let Some(_items) = r.try_take() {
18097|      1|                    pending_mask &= !(1u64 << target_shard);
18098|      1|                }
                              ^0
18099|      1|            }
18100|      2|            check_mask &= check_mask - 1;
18101|       |        }
18102|      1|        assert_eq!(pending_mask, 0b100); // only shard 2 remaining
18103|      1|    }

  607|       |    /// Automated garbage collection for all tombstones older than `ttl_ms` (default: 86_400_000 ms / 24h).
  608|      2|    pub fn gc_tombstones(&mut self, ttl_ms: u64) -> (usize, usize) {
  609|      2|        let now = SystemTime::now()

  611|      2|            .unwrap_or_default()

  613|      2|        let cutoff = now.saturating_sub(ttl_ms);
  614|       |
  615|      2|        let before_regs = self.registers.len();
  616|      2|        self.registers
  617|      2|            .retain(|_, reg| !reg.tombstone || reg.timestamp.physical_ms >= cutoff);
                                           ^1                ^1

  621|      2|        for s in self.sets.values_mut() {

  623|      1|        }
  624|      2|        (reg_pruned, set_pruned)
  625|      2|    }

   50|      9|pub fn encode_geohash(lon: f64, lat: f64) -> Result<u64, &'static str> {
   51|      9|    if lon < GEO_LON_MIN || lon > GEO_LON_MAX {
   52|      0|        return Err("ERR invalid longitude");
   53|      9|    }

   57|       |

   70|    234|        hash |= bit_x << (2 * i);
   71|    234|        hash |= bit_y << (2 * i + 1);

  205|       |/// the bounding box of radius `radius_meters` around (lon, lat).
  206|     12|pub fn geohash_search_ranges(lon: f64, lat: f64, radius_meters: f64) -> Vec<(f64, f64)> {
  207|     12|    if radius_meters <= 0.0 {
  208|      0|        if let Ok(hash) = encode_geohash(lon, lat) {

  221|     12|    let dlon = radius_meters / (111_320.0 * cos_lat);

  244|       |

  447|       |/// Parses a single RESP2/RESP3 frame from `buf` into a `serde_json::Value` and returns `(val, next_pos, is_error)`.
  448|     24|fn parse_resp_frame(buf: &[u8], pos: usize) -> Option<(Value, usize, bool)> {

  760|       |    #[test]
  761|      1|    fn test_sharded_presence_table_bitmask_tracking() {
  762|      1|        let presence = ShardedPresenceTable::new();
  763|      1|        let mut hub_shard0 = PubSubHub::new();
  764|      1|        let mut hub_shard1 = PubSubHub::new();
  765|       |
  766|      1|        let (tx0, _rx0) = flume::bounded(10);
  767|      1|        let (tx1, _rx1) = flume::bounded(10);
  768|       |
  769|       |        // Before any subscriptions, no shards are interested
  770|      1|        assert_eq!(presence.interested_shards(b"sports"), 0);
  771|       |
  772|       |        // Shard 0 subscribes to "sports"
  773|      1|        hub_shard0.subscribe_with_presence(
  774|       |            1,
  775|      1|            Bytes::from_static(b"sports"),
  776|      1|            tx0.clone(),
  777|       |            false,
  778|      1|            Some((0, &presence)),
  779|       |        );
  780|      1|        let mask = presence.interested_shards(b"sports");
  781|      1|        assert_eq!(mask & (1 << 0), 1 << 0, "Shard 0 should be marked present");
  782|      1|        assert_eq!(mask & (1 << 1), 0, "Shard 1 should not be marked present");
  783|       |
  784|       |        // Shard 1 subscribes to "sports" as well
  785|      1|        hub_shard1.subscribe_with_presence(
  786|       |            2,
  787|      1|            Bytes::from_static(b"sports"),
  788|      1|            tx1,
  789|       |            false,
  790|      1|            Some((1, &presence)),
  791|       |        );
  792|      1|        let mask = presence.interested_shards(b"sports");
  793|      1|        assert_eq!(mask & ((1 << 0) | (1 << 1)), (1 << 0) | (1 << 1));
  794|       |
  795|       |        // Shard 0 unsubscribes
  796|      1|        hub_shard0.unsubscribe_with_presence(1, b"sports", Some((0, &presence)));
  797|      1|        let mask = presence.interested_shards(b"sports");
  798|      1|        assert_eq!(mask & (1 << 0), 0, "Shard 0 bit should be cleared");
  799|      1|        assert_eq!(mask & (1 << 1), 1 << 1, "Shard 1 bit should remain");
  800|       |
  801|       |        // Pattern subscription on shard 0 marks pattern presence for all channels
  802|      1|        hub_shard0.psubscribe_with_presence(
  803|       |            3,
  804|      1|            Bytes::from_static(b"news.*"),
  805|      1|            tx0,
  806|       |            false,
  807|      1|            Some((0, &presence)),
  808|       |        );
  809|      1|        assert_eq!(
  810|      1|            presence.interested_shards(b"any_channel") & (1 << 0),
  811|      1|            1 << 0
  812|       |        );
  813|       |

 1182|      1|    fn test_backlog_append_and_diff() {

 1195|      1|        assert!(backlog.can_partial_sync(11, 10));

 1203|      1|        assert_eq!(backlog.get_diff(11, 10), Some(Vec::new()));
 1204|       |

 1213|       |        // target 6 can partial sync (index 0)

 1288|       |

 1363|      1|    fn test_per_shard_parallel_replication_flows() {
 1364|      1|        let hub = ReplicationHub::new(19996);
 1365|      1|        let (tx0, rx0) = flume::bounded(16);
 1366|      1|        let (tx1, rx1) = flume::bounded(16);
 1367|       |
 1368|       |        // Register flows for Shard 0 and Shard 1
 1369|      1|        let flow0 = hub.register_shard_flow(0, 100, tx0);
 1370|      1|        let flow1 = hub.register_shard_flow(1, 101, tx1);
 1371|       |
 1372|      1|        assert!(hub.has_shard_flows.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 1373|      1|        assert_eq!(flow0.shard_id, 0);
 1374|      1|        assert_eq!(flow1.shard_id, 1);
 1375|       |
 1376|       |        // Mutation on Shard 0
 1377|      1|        let cmd0 = b"*3\r\n$3\r\nSET\r\n$4\r\nkey0\r\n$4\r\nval0\r\n";
 1378|      1|        hub.propagate_shard(0, cmd0);
 1379|       |
 1380|       |        // Shard 0 flow receives mutation, Shard 1 receives nothing
 1381|      1|        assert_eq!(rx0.try_recv().unwrap(), cmd0.to_vec());
 1382|      1|        assert!(rx1.try_recv().is_err());
 1383|      1|        assert_eq!(flow0.lsn.load(Ordering::Relaxed), cmd0.len() as u64);
 1384|      1|        assert_eq!(flow1.lsn.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 0);
 1385|       |
 1386|       |        // Mutation on Shard 1
 1387|      1|        let cmd1 = b"*3\r\n$3\r\nSET\r\n$4\r\nkey1\r\n$4\r\nval1\r\n";
 1388|      1|        hub.propagate_shard(1, cmd1);
 1389|       |
 1390|       |        // Shard 1 flow receives mutation, Shard 0 receives nothing
 1391|      1|        assert_eq!(rx1.try_recv().unwrap(), cmd1.to_vec());
 1392|      1|        assert!(rx0.try_recv().is_err());
 1393|      1|        assert_eq!(flow1.lsn.load(Ordering::Relaxed), cmd1.len() as u64);
 1394|       |
 1395|       |        // Test ACK tracking
 1396|      1|        hub.update_shard_flow_ack(0, 100, 42);
 1397|      1|        assert_eq!(flow0.ack_lsn.load(Ordering::Relaxed), 42);
 1398|       |

 1400|      1|        hub.unregister_shard_flow(0, 100);
 1401|      1|        hub.unregister_shard_flow(1, 101);
 1402|      1|        assert!(!hub.has_shard_flows.load(Ordering::Relaxed));
 1403|      1|    }

 4185|      1|    fn test_begin_mget_mset_dispatch_without_blocking() {
 4186|      1|        let num_shards = 4;
 4187|      1|        let (mut senders_mesh, _receivers) = crate::mailbox::create_shard_mesh(num_shards);
 4188|      1|        let senders = senders_mesh.remove(0);
 4189|      1|        let db0 = Rc::new(RefCell::new(crate::shard::ShardDb::new(9997)));
 4190|      1|        let router = Router::new(
 4191|       |            0,
 4192|      1|            num_shards,
 4193|       |            9997,
 4194|      1|            db0,
 4195|      1|            senders,
 4196|      1|            None,
 4197|      1|            Rc::new(RefCell::new(crate::pubsub::PubSubHub::new())),
 4198|      1|            std::env::temp_dir(),
 4199|       |        );
 4200|       |
 4201|       |        // Pick one key owned by this shard and one owned by a peer shard.
 4202|      1|        let mut local_key = None;
 4203|      1|        let mut remote_key = None;
 4204|      2|        for i in 0..1000 {
                               ^1
 4205|      2|            let k = Bytes::from(format!("split_k_{i}"));
 4206|      2|            if router.target_shard(&k) == 0 {
 4207|      1|                if local_key.is_none() {
 4208|      1|                    local_key = Some(k);
 4209|      1|                }
                              ^0
 4210|      1|            } else if remote_key.is_none() {
 4211|      1|                remote_key = Some(k);
 4212|      1|            }
                          ^0
 4213|      2|            if local_key.is_some() && remote_key.is_some() {
                                                    ^1         ^1
 4214|      1|                break;
 4215|      1|            }
 4216|       |        }
 4217|      1|        let local_key = local_key.expect("no key hashed to shard 0");
 4218|      1|        let remote_key = remote_key.expect("no key hashed to a peer shard");
 4219|       |
 4220|      1|        router
 4221|      1|            .local_db
 4222|      1|            .borrow_mut()
 4223|      1|            .set(local_key.clone(), Bytes::from_static(b"v1"), None);
 4224|       |
 4225|      1|        let mut rt = monoio::RuntimeBuilder::<monoio::FusionDriver>::new()
 4226|      1|            .enable_all()
 4227|      1|            .build()
 4228|      1|            .unwrap();
 4229|       |
 4230|      1|        rt.block_on(async move {
 4231|       |            // All keys local: served inline, no in-flight handle, reply already written.
 4232|      1|            let mut out = Vec::new();
 4233|      1|            let inflight = router
 4234|      1|                .begin_mget_resp(vec![local_key.clone()], &mut out)
 4235|      1|                .await;
 4236|      1|            assert!(inflight.is_none());
 4237|      1|            assert_eq!(out, b"*1\r\n$2\r\nv1\r\n".to_vec());
 4238|       |
 4239|       |            // Cross-shard: dispatch returns immediately with a pending shard and
 4240|       |            // writes nothing, leaving serialization to the gather phase.
 4241|      1|            let mut out = Vec::new();
 4242|      1|            let inflight = router
 4243|      1|                .begin_mget_resp(vec![local_key, remote_key.clone()], &mut out)
 4244|      1|                .await
 4245|      1|                .expect("cross-shard mget must yield an in-flight handle");
 4246|      1|            assert!(out.is_empty());
 4247|      1|            assert_eq!(inflight.descriptor.pending.load(Ordering::Acquire), 1);
 4248|      1|            assert_eq!(inflight.total_keys, 2);
 4249|      1|            drop(inflight);
 4250|       |
 4251|       |            // MSET dispatches the same way.
 4252|      1|            let inflight = router
 4253|      1|                .begin_mset(vec![(remote_key, Bytes::from_static(b"v2"))])
 4254|      1|                .expect("cross-shard mset must yield an in-flight handle");
 4255|      1|            assert_eq!(inflight.descriptor.pending.load(Ordering::Acquire), 1);
 4256|      1|        });
 4257|      1|    }

  599|       |/// Serialize Slowlog entries into RESP2 format
  600|      3|pub fn write_slowlog_entries_resp(entries: &[SlowlogEntry], out: &mut Vec<u8>) {
  601|      3|    out.extend_from_slice(format!("*{}\r\n", entries.len()).as_bytes());
  602|      3|    for e in entries {
                      ^2
  603|       |        // Redis 7.2 returns 7 elements: [id, timestamp, duration_us, argv, client_addr, client_name, original_argc]
  604|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(b"*7\r\n");
  605|       |        // 0. ID
  606|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(format!(":{}\r\n", e.id).as_bytes());
  607|       |        // 1. Timestamp
  608|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(format!(":{}\r\n", e.timestamp).as_bytes());
  609|       |        // 2. Duration (us)
  610|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(format!(":{}\r\n", e.duration_us).as_bytes());
  611|       |        // 3. Arguments Array
  612|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(format!("*{}\r\n", e.argv.len()).as_bytes());
  613|      6|        for arg in &e.argv {

  614|      6|            out.extend_from_slice(format!("${}\r\n", arg.len()).as_bytes());
  615|      6|            out.extend_from_slice(arg);
  616|      6|            out.extend_from_slice(b"\r\n");
  617|      6|        }
  618|       |        // 4. Client Address
  619|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(
  620|      2|            format!("${}\r\n{}\r\n", e.client_addr.len(), e.client_addr).as_bytes(),
  621|       |        );
  622|       |        // 5. Client Name
  623|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(
  624|      2|            format!("${}\r\n{}\r\n", e.client_name.len(), e.client_name).as_bytes(),
  625|       |        );
  626|       |        // 6. Original Argc
  627|      2|        out.extend_from_slice(format!(":{}\r\n", e.original_argc).as_bytes());

 8997|       |    /// Bounded background sampling of hash field expirations (`HEXPIRE`).
 8998|       |    /// Samples up to `max_keys` entries from `hash_field_expires` starting at `sample_cursor`
 8999|       |    /// and reclaims expired fields (and parent hashes when empty).
 9000|     98|    pub fn evict_expired_hash_fields_sample(&mut self, max_keys: usize) -> usize {
 9001|     98|        if self.hash_field_expires.is_empty() || max_keys == 0 {
 9002|      0|            return 0;
 9003|     98|        }
 9004|     98|        let now = Instant::now();
 9005|     98|        let total = self.hash_field_expires.len();

 9008|     98|            .hash_field_expires
 9009|     98|            .keys()
 9010|     98|            .skip(start)
 9011|     98|            .chain(self.hash_field_expires.keys().take(start))
 9012|     98|            .take(max_keys)
 9013|     98|            .cloned()
 9014|     98|            .collect();
 9015|       |

 9017|     98|        for key in sample_keys {

 9019|     98|            let mut empty_map = false;
 9020|     98|            if let Some(fmap) = self.hash_field_expires.get_mut(&key) {
 9021|     98|                fmap.retain(|f, exp| {
 9022|     98|                    if now >= *exp {
 9023|      0|                        expired.push(f.clone());
 9024|      0|                        false
 9025|       |                    } else {
 9026|     98|                        true
 9027|       |                    }
 9028|     98|                });
 9029|     98|                empty_map = fmap.is_empty();
 9030|      0|            }
 9031|     98|            if empty_map {
 9032|      0|                self.hash_field_expires.remove(&key);
 9033|     98|            }
 9034|     98|            if !expired.is_empty() {
 9035|      0|                evicted_fields += expired.len();
 9036|      0|                let _ = self.hdel(&key, &expired);
 9037|     98|            }
 9038|       |        }
 9039|     98|        evicted_fields
 9040|     98|    }

12727|       |    #[test]
12728|      1|    fn test_three_state_lifecycle_and_instant_decommit() {
12729|      1|        let mut table = RudisTable::new();
12730|      1|        let initial_mem = table.used_memory;
12731|       |
12732|       |        // 1. Hot key
12733|      1|        table.set(
12734|      1|            Bytes::from_static(b"k1"),
12735|      1|            Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"),
12736|      1|            None,
12737|       |        );
12738|      1|        assert!(table.used_memory > initial_mem);
12739|      1|        let hot_mem = table.used_memory;
12740|      1|        assert_eq!(
12741|      1|            table.get(b"k1").unwrap(),
12742|      1|            Some(Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"))
12743|       |        );
12744|       |
12745|       |        // 2. Transition Hot -> Cooled
12746|      1|        let ptr = TieredPointer {
12747|      1|            file_id: 0,
12748|      1|            offset: 4096,
12749|      1|            length: 128,
12750|      1|            value_type: 0,
12751|      1|        };
12752|      1|        assert!(table.set_cooled_pointer(b"k1", ptr));
12753|      1|        assert!(table.is_cooled(b"k1").is_some());
12754|      1|        assert!(table.is_tiered(b"k1").is_none());
12755|       |
12756|       |        // Fast DRAM hit on Cooled key
12757|      1|        assert_eq!(
12758|      1|            table.get(b"k1").unwrap(),
12759|      1|            Some(Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"))
12760|       |        );
12761|      1|        let (entry_val, _) = table.get_entry(b"k1").unwrap();
12762|      1|        assert_eq!(
12763|       |            entry_val,
12764|      1|            RudisValue::String(Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"))
12765|       |        );
12766|       |
12767|       |        // 3. Instant Zero-I/O Decommit: Cooled -> Cold (Tiered)
12768|      1|        let (p, freed) = table.decommit_cooled_key(b"k1").unwrap();
12769|      1|        assert_eq!(p.offset, 4096);
12770|      1|        assert!(freed > 0);
12771|      1|        assert!(table.used_memory < hot_mem);
12772|      1|        assert!(table.is_cooled(b"k1").is_none());
12773|      1|        assert!(table.is_tiered(b"k1").is_some());
12774|       |
12775|       |        // 4. Restore Cold -> Cooled (Read hit)
12776|      1|        let restored_val = RudisValue::String(Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"));
12777|      1|        assert!(table.restore_tiered_value(b"k1", restored_val));
12778|      1|        assert!(table.is_cooled(b"k1").is_some());
12779|      1|        assert_eq!(
12780|      1|            table.get(b"k1").unwrap(),
12781|      1|            Some(Bytes::from_static(b"hello_tiered_storage_world"))
12782|       |        );
12783|       |
12784|       |        // 5. Decommit all cooled
12785|      1|        let (count, total_freed) = table.decommit_all_cooled();
12786|      1|        assert_eq!(count, 1);
12787|      1|        assert!(total_freed > 0);
12788|      1|        assert!(table.is_tiered(b"k1").is_some());
12789|      1|        assert!(table.is_cooled(b"k1").is_none());
12790|      1|    }

                               ^1

12928|    490|        }

12937|      1|        assert_eq!(table.len(), 10);
12938|       |
12939|       |        // Verify remaining 10 keys are intact
12940|     10|        for i in 490..500 {
                               ^1
12941|     10|            assert_eq!(
12942|     10|                table.get(format!("key_{}", i).as_bytes()).unwrap(),
12943|     10|                Some(Bytes::from(format!("val_{}", i)))

  257|       |    /// Read a 4KB page from disk with coalescing.

 2877|       |    /// Queries the semantic cache for the closest non-expired entry matching `scope` whose
 2878|       |    /// cosine similarity is `>= threshold`.
 2879|     10|    pub fn get(
 2880|     10|        &mut self,
 2881|     10|        query: &[f32],
 2882|     10|        threshold: f32,
 2883|     10|        scope: Option<&[u8]>,
 2884|     10|    ) -> Result<Option<SemanticHit>, String> {
 2885|     10|        self.purge_expired();
 2886|     10|        if self.entries.is_empty() {
 2887|      0|            self.misses += 1;
 2888|      0|            return Ok(None);
 2889|     10|        }
 2890|     10|        if query.len() != self.index.dim {
 2891|      0|            return Err("ERR vector dimension mismatch".to_string());
 2892|     10|        }
 2893|     10|        let entries_ref = &self.entries;
 2894|     10|        let filter_fn = |key: &Bytes| -> bool {
 2895|     10|            let Some(entry) = entries_ref.get(key) else {
 2896|      0|                return false;
 2897|       |            };
 2898|     10|            if let Some(req_scope) = scope {
 2899|     10|                entry.scope.as_deref() == Some(req_scope)
 2900|       |            } else {
 2901|      0|                true
 2902|       |            }
 2903|     10|        };
 2904|     10|        let candidates = self
 2905|     10|            .index
 2906|     10|            .search_filtered(query, 4, None, true, Some(&filter_fn));
 2907|     10|        if let Some((best_id, dist)) = candidates.into_iter().next() {
                                   ^8       ^8
 2908|      8|            let sim = (1.0 - dist).clamp(0.0, 1.0);
 2909|      8|            if sim >= threshold
 2910|      6|                && let Some(entry) = self.entries.get(&best_id)
 2911|       |            {
 2912|      6|                self.hits += 1;
 2913|      6|                self.tokens_saved += entry.tokens;
 2914|      6|                return Ok(Some(SemanticHit {
 2915|      6|                    id: entry.id.clone(),
 2916|      6|                    prompt: entry.prompt.clone(),
 2917|      6|                    response: entry.response.clone(),
 2918|      6|                    score: sim,
 2919|      6|                }));
 2920|      2|            }
 2921|      2|        }
 2922|      4|        self.misses += 1;
 2923|      4|        Ok(None)
 2924|     10|    }

 2929|      4|        let removed_vec = self.index.remove(id);
 2930|      4|        removed_entry || removed_vec
                                       ^2
 2931|      4|    }

 3223|      1|    fn test_pq_kmeans_codebook_training_reduces_distortion() {
 3224|       |        // Generate vectors in a non-unit scale [10.0, 50.0] where an untrained [-1, 1] codebook
 3225|       |        // suffers high clamping distortion, and verify k-means++ + Lloyd training drastically
 3226|       |        // lowers reconstruction error and auto-trains on HnswIndex.
 3227|      1|        let mut samples = Vec::new();
 3228|     24|        for i in 0..24 {
                               ^1
 3229|     24|            let base = 10.0 + (i as f32) * 1.5;
 3230|     24|            samples.push(vec![
 3231|     24|                base,
 3232|     24|                base + 2.0,
 3233|     24|                base * 0.5,
 3234|     24|                base - 3.0,
 3235|     24|                -base,
 3236|     24|                base + 5.0,
 3237|     24|                base * 1.2,
 3238|     24|                base + 0.25,
 3239|     24|            ]);
 3240|     24|        }
 3241|      1|        let untrained = ProductQuantizer::new(8, 2);
 3242|      1|        let trained = ProductQuantizer::train(8, 2, &samples, 15);
 3243|      1|        let err_untrained = untrained.distortion(&samples);
 3244|      1|        let err_trained = trained.distortion(&samples);
 3245|      1|        assert!(
 3246|      1|            err_trained < err_untrained * 0.01,
 3247|       |            "expected trained PQ distortion ({err_trained}) << untrained ({err_untrained})"
 3248|       |        );
 3249|       |
 3250|      1|        let mut idx = HnswIndex::new("pq_auto".to_string(), 8, VectorMetric::L2);
 3251|     24|        for (i, v) in samples.iter().enumerate() {
                                    ^1             ^1
 3252|     24|            idx.add_quantized_ext(Bytes::from(format!("p{i}")), v.clone(), false, true, false)
 3253|     24|                .unwrap();
 3254|     24|        }
 3255|      1|        assert!(idx.pq_trained);
 3256|      1|        let hits = idx.search(&samples[10], 1);
 3257|      1|        assert_eq!(hits[0].0, Bytes::from("p10"));

  198|       |    /// Attempts zero-copy send on a socket using `MSG_ZEROCOPY`.
  199|       |    /// Falls back to standard non-blocking `send` if the kernel buffer is full or unsupported.
  200|      2|    pub fn send_zc(&self, fd: RawFd, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<usize> {
  201|      2|        if data.is_empty() {
  202|      0|            return Ok(0);
  203|      2|        }
  204|       |
  205|       |        // According to Linux kernel docs, zero-copy incurs page-locking overhead,
  206|       |        // so MSG_ZEROCOPY is optimal for payloads >= 4 KB.
  207|      2|        let flags = if data.len() >= PAGE_SIZE {
  208|      0|            libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL | MSG_ZEROCOPY
  209|       |        } else {
  210|      2|            libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL
  211|       |        };
  212|       |
  213|      2|        let ret =
  214|      2|            unsafe { libc::send(fd, data.as_ptr() as *const libc::c_void, data.len(), flags) };
  215|       |
  216|      2|        if ret >= 0 {
  217|      2|            let sent = ret as usize;
  218|      2|            self.stats.zc_send_calls.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  219|      2|            self.stats
  220|      2|                .zc_bytes_sent
  221|      2|                .fetch_add(sent as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
  222|      2|            Ok(sent)
  223|       |        } else {
  224|      0|            let err = io::Error::last_os_error();
  225|       |            // Fall back to standard send on ENOBUFS or if MSG_ZEROCOPY is not supported
  226|      0|            if err.raw_os_error() == Some(libc::ENOBUFS) || flags & MSG_ZEROCOPY != 0 {
  227|      0|                self.stats.fallback_sends.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
  228|      0|                let fallback_ret = unsafe {
  229|      0|                    libc::send(
  230|      0|                        fd,
  231|      0|                        data.as_ptr() as *const libc::c_void,
  232|      0|                        data.len(),
  233|       |                        libc::MSG_NOSIGNAL,
  234|       |                    )
  235|       |                };
  236|      0|                if fallback_ret >= 0 {
  237|      0|                    let sent = fallback_ret as usize;
  238|      0|                    self.stats
  239|      0|                        .zc_bytes_sent
  240|      0|                        .fetch_add(sent as u64, Ordering::Relaxed);
  241|      0|                    return Ok(sent);
  242|      0|                }
  243|      0|            }
  244|      0|            Err(err)
  245|       |        }
  246|      2|    }
